liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Throwing Stones** (2 other sources): Throwing Stones ends with a Mind Left Body tease; Throwing Stones closes with a Mind Left Body tease [7][13]
- **Black Peter** (2 reviews): Black Peter has no solo because Jerry was eager to get to Goin' Down the Road; Jerry repeatedly plays the Black Throated Wind lick in the jam leading into Black Peter [21][22]
- **Bertha** (1 review): The show opens with a Bertha into Promised Land pairing [22]
- **West L.A. Fadeaway** (1 review): Jerry has a very strong guitar tone on West L.A. Fadeaway [22]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): China Cat into Rider closed the first set [18]
- **Help On The Way** (1 review): Help on the Way into Slipknot is short but blazing, with soulful singing and noodling from Jerry [24]
- **Slipknot!** (1 review): Slipknot is short but wild, and gets the second set rolling [20]
- **Truckin'** (1 other source): Truckin' is followed by Smokestack Lightning and Other One teases [13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Smokestack Lightnin' Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **The Other One Jam**: back after 111 archived shows (587 days) [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-04-09.mtx.seamons.97109.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 141 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1983-04-09.163634.senn441.neumann.u87.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 148 min [2]
- **gd1983-04-09.141613.beyerm201.executive-crew.holbrook.flac2448**: audience recording; 22 songs; 143 min [4]. Said about its sound: The master is noted as distorted for most of one song [4]
- **gd83-04-09.sbd.miller.27703.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 141 min; rated 4.27/5 by 22 [6]. Said about its sound: Vocals are sweet and the mix has great separation between instruments; Vocals sit a bit high in the mix, and Brent sounds great throughout; On this board Brent is too loud in Brown Eyed Women, and Phil's bombs are hard to hear in Bertha [23][26][28]
- **gd1983-04-09.sbd.miller.93145.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 140 min; rated 3.62/5 by 8 [7]
- **gd83-04-09.senn421.cribbs.9199.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 140 min; rated 3.25/5 by 8 [10]. Said about its sound: Audience tapes capture the intensity of Phil's bass bombs, though the reviewer wishes for a really good audience tape [21]
- **gd1983-04-09.145467.fob.nak700.cohen.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 144 min [13]

## Around the show

- The reviewer traveled to this show as the first show they ever travelled to see [18]
- A 17-year-old on a first road trip felt the scene was intimate, before the huge parking-lot era [26]
- Reviewer was at college in Boston and heard excited reports as the tour moved north [28]
- This opened the East Coast tour that year, and the crowd went wild when the second set began [29]
- House lights came on after Saturday Night, so the tapers began packing up and missed the first seconds of Satisfaction [4]
- The second set starts promisingly but fizzles out before the end [20]
- The 1983-84 era is underrated; the setlists look weak on paper but the playing was exploratory [23]
- West L.A. Fadeaway and My Brother Esau were early versions of those songs [24]
- Hampton has a Smokestack tradition; no other venue got it twice [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-04-09.mtx.seamons.97109.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix of SBD (shnid=93145):AUD (shnid=14190): [1]
- **gd1983-04-09.163634.senn441.neumann.u87.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob, Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) Sennheiser 441's (left + right) + (1) Neumann U87 (center) > Nakamichi 550 [2]. Also: Rob Eaton made the recording and transfer; Charlie Miller coordinated the release; A Nakamichi 700 source from Bob Wagner supplies a 1:21 patch in Drums [2]
- **gd1983-04-09.141613.beyerm201.executive-crew.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew: Kyle Holbrook, Olvy Johnson, Mike Yacavone, Tom Pinney; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: flac24/48 Source Audience Recording: Beyer M 201c Location: 60 feet from stage|DFC [4]
- **gd83-04-09.sbd.miller.27703.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> Master Cassette> Reel> Dat (48k) [6]
- **gd1983-04-09.sbd.miller.93145.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette [7]. Also: Remaster of shnid 27703 from a Sennheiser 441 front-of-board cassette master via DAT; channels swapped in set one were fixed; Rob Eaton's recording supplies patches for Truckin' and One More Saturday Night [7]
- **gd83-04-09.senn421.cribbs.9199.sbeok.shnf**: source: Senn 421 mics > Sony TC-D5 > MAC > DAT > CD [10]
- **gd1983-04-09.145467.fob.nak700.cohen.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Cohen; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Cohen's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5 [13]

The band hadn't played Smokestack in ages; the jam was a treat but frustrating because nobody sang it
China Cat into Rider closed the first set
The second set starts promisingly but fizzles out before the end
Slipknot is short but wild, and gets the second set rolling

Black Peter has no solo because Jerry was eager to get to Goin' Down the Road
Satisfaction is called insanely hot

Jerry repeatedly plays the Black Throated Wind lick in the jam leading into Black Peter
The show opens with a Bertha into Promised Land pairing
Vocals are sweet and the mix has great separation between instruments
The 1983-84 era is underrated; the setlists look weak on paper but the playing was exploratory
West L.A. Fadeaway and My Brother Esau were early versions of those songs
Help on the Way into Slipknot is short but blazing, with soulful singing and noodling from Jerry
Hampton has a Smokestack tradition; no other venue got it twice
A 17-year-old on a first road trip felt the scene was intimate, before the huge parking-lot era
This was among the first shows with Phil on six-string bass, and he dropped bombs early
Vocals sit a bit high in the mix, and Brent sounds great throughout
Recommends the 1983 Poplar Creek show as another old-school early-80s show

Reviewer was at college in Boston and heard excited reports as the tour moved north
